title: Base change for extension by zero
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-dc-open-base-change-morphism], assume that the square is
cartesian, i.e. $X'=X\times_ZZ'=g^{-1}(X)$. Then the exchange morphism
$\mathrm{Ex}^{j}_{sq}\colon j'_!\circ Lg'^*\to Lg^*\circ j_!$ is an isomorphism, for every
commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$.

proof.text: Put $A=j'_!\circ Lg'^*$, $B=Lg^*\circ j_!$, and let $\alpha:A\to B$ be the exchange of the current [def-sfb-dc-open-base-change-morphism]. Explicitly its component is $\alpha_K=\varepsilon'_{Lg^*j_!K}\circ j'_!(\theta_{j_!K})\circ j'_!Lg'^*(\eta_K)$, where $\theta$ is $Lg'^*Lj^*\xrightarrow{c_{g',j}^{-1}}L(j\circ g')^*=L(g\circ j')^*\xrightarrow{c_{j',g}}Lj'^*Lg^*$. This is the comparison for the square with $j'$ on top and $g',g$ vertical, as specified in that definition; no derived-pushforward preservation hypothesis is needed. The setting supplies a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $k$-morphisms, and any commutative condensed ring $\Lambda$. The square is cartesian and both vertical arrows are open immersions. Thus [stage3-sfb-open-base-change-component-mono] applies to this exact unit-square-counit transformation: its equality hypothesis is reflexivity after using the displayed formula (diagrammatic $g'^*\mathbin{\gg}j'_!$ means $j'_!\circ Lg'^*$). It gives that $\alpha_K:A(K)\to B(K)$ is monic for every $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Under the same hypotheses, [stage3-sfb-open-base-change-component-section] gives for each $K$ a map $\beta_K:B(K)\to A(K)$ with $\alpha_K\circ\beta_K=1_{B(K)}$ (the statement's $\beta_K\gg\alpha_K=1$ uses diagrammatic composition). Hence $\alpha_K\circ(\beta_K\circ\alpha_K)=(\alpha_K\circ\beta_K)\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_K=\alpha_K\circ1_{A(K)}$. Cancel the monomorphism $\alpha_K$ from step 1 to obtain $\beta_K\circ\alpha_K=1_{A(K)}$. Thus $\beta_K$ is a two-sided inverse. It is unique: if $\gamma_K$ is another such inverse, then $\gamma_K=\gamma_K\circ(\alpha_K\circ\beta_K)=(\gamma_K\circ\alpha_K)\circ\beta_K=\beta_K$. No assumption about naturality of the sections has been used.

source.place: Theorem thm-sfb-dc-open-base-change-iso. The blueprint proof (thm-sfb-dc-open-base-change-iso.proof.md: reduction to the underived exchange j'_!g'^*M -> g^*j_!M and its mate j^*g_* -> g'_*j'^*, via units outside this unit's uses) is not followed; this step follows the landed Lean argument (MorphismDefs.lean, boundedConstructibleOpenImmersionLowerShriekBaseChange_leftInverse) through the same-unit component-mono and component-section statements (agent argument).

proof.text: Take the unique inverses $\beta_K$ from step 2. For a morphism $u:K\to L$, naturality of $\alpha$ gives $B(u)\circ\alpha_K=\alpha_L\circ A(u)$. Multiply this equality on the left by $\beta_L$ and on the right by $\beta_K$; the two inverse equations reduce it to $\beta_L\circ B(u)=A(u)\circ\beta_K$. These are exactly the naturality equations for $\beta:B\to A$. Both composites $\alpha\circ\beta$ and $\beta\circ\alpha$ are identities because their components are the identities proved in step 2. Therefore the specified exchange $\alpha=\mathrm{Ex}^{j}_{sq}$ is a natural isomorphism, for every $\Lambda$ in the statement.
